sessionTitle: Embracing frontier R&D with Microsoft Discovery

announcements.name: General availability of Microsoft Discovery
announcements.shortDescription: The enterprise platform, introduced in private preview at last year's Build, has moved to general availability
announcements.longDescription: Microsoft Discovery is an enterprise platform for what the speaker calls "frontier R&D," using agentic AI to let teams of AI agents execute the scientific discovery loop end to end while humans provide intent, direction, guardrails, and judgment. Introduced in private preview at last year's Build, it has now moved to general availability. The team shared Build demos including developing novel PFAS-free immersion coolants [inferred] and breaking down plastics using proteins for recycling.

announcements.name: Microsoft Discovery app (free download)
announcements.shortDescription: A lightweight local on-ramp to frontier R&D that requires only a GitHub Copilot license and no Azure account to get started
announcements.longDescription: The Microsoft Discovery app is a lightweight, free on-ramp to frontier R&D that complements the core enterprise services. It is a free download that only requires a GitHub Copilot license to get started, and does not need an Azure account, though having one provides access to enterprise services. It is positioned to reduce the friction of configuring Azure resources and dealing with IT compliance for those who just want to explore agentic discovery.

announcements.name: Discovery Engine
announcements.shortDescription: A cognitive layer that fully automates the discovery loop (hypothesis, experimentation, reasoning), spawning and assigning tasks to agents and abandoning or continuing research paths based on model confidence scores
announcements.longDescription: The Discovery Engine is one of three new capabilities added for scientific research, and it fully automates the scientific discovery loop of hypothesis, experimentation, and reasoning. It can run locally in the Discovery app, and with an Azure account it is also supported as an enterprise service running in the cloud, accessible via the browser. It works alongside the bookshelf and the scientific research-tailored user experience.

announcements.name: Bookshelf with GraphRAG
announcements.shortDescription: A graph-based information retrieval system that indexes scientific papers using entity-relationship graph structures rather than a traditional vector store, productizing GraphRAG technology from Microsoft Research
announcements.longDescription: The bookshelf is a graph-based information retrieval system, one of three new capabilities added for scientific research in Microsoft Discovery. It can run locally in the app, and with an Azure account it is also available as an enterprise service running in the cloud and accessible from the browser. The user experience is described as familiar because Discovery is built on Visual Studio Code and GitHub Copilot [inferred].
